events.title: The Swedish warship Vasa sinks on her maiden voyage
events.description: Top-heavy and unstable, the warship Vasa heeled over in a gust and sank in Stockholm harbour less than a mile into her first voyage. Raised in 1961, she is now a celebrated museum ship.
events.html: Top-heavy and unstable, the warship Vasa heeled over in a gust and sank in Stockholm harbour less than a mile into her first voyage. Raised in 1961, she is now a celebrated museum ship.

events.title: Insurgents storm the Tuileries Palace in Paris
events.description: Armed Parisians and provincial volunteers attacked the Tuileries, killing hundreds of the Swiss Guards. Louis XVI was suspended and imprisoned, and the French monarchy fell weeks later.
events.html: Armed Parisians and provincial volunteers attacked the Tuileries, killing hundreds of the Swiss Guards. Louis XVI was suspended and imprisoned, and the French monarchy fell weeks later.

events.title: The Louvre opens as a public museum
events.description: The revolutionary government opened the Muséum central des arts in the former royal palace, on the first anniversary of the monarchy's fall. The Louvre became one of the world's greatest museums.
events.html: The revolutionary government opened the Muséum central des arts in the former royal palace, on the first anniversary of the monarchy's fall. The Louvre became one of the world's greatest museums.

events.title: Quito's patriots depose the Spanish authorities
events.description: Criollo leaders in Quito overthrew the royal president and formed a governing junta, one of the first such moves in Spanish South America. It was crushed, but Ecuador won independence in 1822.

events.title: Congress establishes the Smithsonian Institution
events.description: President Polk signed the act creating the Smithsonian, funded by the bequest of British chemist James Smithson. It grew into the world's largest museum, education and research complex.

events.title: Japan offers to surrender if the Emperor is preserved
events.description: After an imperial intervention, Japan told the Allies it would accept the Potsdam terms provided the Emperor's prerogatives were kept. The US reply left his status to the Allied commander and the Japanese people.
